newsitem.title: USA: Morgan Stanley's Biggs underweighs U.S. - Fortune.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Stanley's Biggs underweighs U.S. - Fortune.

text.p: Morgan Stanley's director of global strategy Barton Biggs is recommending an underweighting in U.S. and European equities and a slight overweighting in Japanese equities, Fortune magazine reported in its "Investors Guide '97" issue.

Biggs is suggesting that investors put a third of their worldwide equities investments into U.S. stocks, the magazine reported. U.S. equities represent about 40 percent of the value of the world's stock markets.
European equities would represent about 19 percent of his portfolio, versus an index weight of 26 percent, Biggs told the magazine.

Japanese equities would consist of 22 percent of a world equities portfolio, despite an index of 19 percent of the value of the world's equities, the magazine said. Biggs said he favors small and mid-cap Japanese firms and advises investors to use mutual funds to invest in Japan.
The rally in U.S. stocks have forced him to underweight them in his portfolio, the magazine reported.

European stocks will be hurt short-term in the continent's push for the European Monetary Union, Biggs told the magazine. The move toward a unified currency will lead to higher taxes and reduced spending in the short-term, he told the magazine.
The balance of his model global equities portfolio would be placed in emerging markets, such as Russia, Brazil, South Korea or India, Biggs told Fortune.
